newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ domestic, vehicle insurance claims rising.
newsitem.headline: NZ domestic, vehicle insurance claims rising.

text.p: Claims are on the increase for domestic home and contents insurance and private and commercial motor vehicle insurance, the Insurance Council of New Zealand said on Thursday.
Council chief executive David Sargeant said the trend in both categories over the last five years showed a deteriorating result for insurers.
"Claims have increased in both number and cost, in proportion to the premium being collected," he said.
"The reports we are getting from companies indicate that the Auckland region is the biggest trouble spot, with a much higher incidence of claim and cost of claim."

Sargeant said burglaries and the high cost of motor vehicle repairs were a major problem. Indications were that in the last year burglaries comprised up to 28 percent of home and contents claims, and represented 50 percent of claims closts.

He said insurers were often using imported goods, such as car parts in motor vehicle repairs, and given the strong New Zealand dollar the council would have expected the cost of claims to be going down, not up. It intends to investigate why the cost of claims is rising.
